rules.quote: Every branch is tied to an issue — open the issue first, then create the branch from it.
rules.rule: Before creating any branch, open an issue for the work first, then create the branch from that issue.

rules.quote: Phase work: `phase-N-short-description` (e.g. `phase-8-group-gifts`)
rules.rule: Name phase work branches as `phase-N-short-description`.

rules.quote: Bug fixes: decide the name based on the issue (e.g. `fix-share-url` or `fix/share-url`) — no rigid convention, just keep it descriptive
rules.rule: Name bug fix branches descriptively based on the issue, with no rigid convention.

rules.quote: Always branch from `Development` unless the user explicitly says otherwise.
rules.rule: Create branches from `Development` unless the user explicitly instructs otherwise.

rules.quote: Never branch from `main`.
rules.rule: Never create a branch from `main`.

rules.quote: All branches PR into `Development`.
rules.rule: Open pull requests for all branches targeting `Development`.

rules.quote: Only `Development` ever PRs into `main`.
rules.rule: Only `Development` may be used to open a pull request into `main`.

rules.quote: No other branch types — no `infra/`, `docs/`, `chore/` etc.
rules.rule: Do not create branch types other than phase work and bug fix branches (no `infra/`, `docs/`, `chore/` prefixes).

rules.quote: Flag them and ask the user before deleting.
rules.rule: When stale branches are found, flag them and ask the user before deleting any of them.

rules.quote: Never delete a branch unilaterally unless it was just merged as part of the release cleanup checklist.
rules.rule: Never delete a branch on your own initiative, except branches just merged as part of the release cleanup checklist.

rules.quote: After spotting stale branches via `git branch -r`, list them and ask the user which to delete
rules.rule: After spotting stale branches via `git branch -r`, list them and ask the user which to delete.

rules.quote: `git push origin --delete <branch>` only after user confirms or as part of post-release cleanup
rules.rule: Run `git push origin --delete <branch>` only after the user confirms or as part of post-release cleanup.

rules.quote: Conventional commits with a type prefix, imperative subject, optional why-body.
rules.rule: Format every commit message as a conventional commit: a type prefix, an imperative subject, and an optional body explaining why.

rules.quote: `feat:` — new feature or phase work
rules.rule: Use the `feat:` prefix for commits that add a new feature or phase work.

rules.quote: `fix:` — bug fix
rules.rule: Use the `fix:` prefix for commits that fix a bug.

rules.quote: `chore:` — version bumps, config, dependencies
rules.rule: Use the `chore:` prefix for commits that bump versions, change config, or change dependencies.

rules.quote: `docs:` — design docs, README, CHANGELOG only
rules.rule: Use the `docs:` prefix only for commits that change design docs, the README, or the CHANGELOG.

rules.quote: `refactor:` — code change, no behaviour change
rules.rule: Use the `refactor:` prefix for code changes that do not change behaviour.

rules.quote: **CHANGELOG:** Update on every commit — no exceptions, including typo fixes and chores.
rules.rule: Update CHANGELOG.md on every commit, with no exceptions, including typo fixes and chores.

rules.quote: Do **not** bump manually.
rules.rule: Do not manually bump the version in package.json.

rules.quote: do not preemptively bump `package.json` on feature branches.
rules.rule: Do not preemptively bump package.json on feature branches.

rules.quote: fix `.github/release-please-manifest.json` to match the latest shipped tag
rules.rule: If the Release Please manifest drifts after an out-of-band release, fix .github/release-please-manifest.json to match the latest shipped tag.

rules.quote: If one entry is enormous or automation stalls, flag the user — do not delete history silently.
rules.rule: If a CHANGELOG entry is enormous or CHANGELOG compaction automation stalls, flag it to the user and do not delete history silently.

rules.quote: Every commit: update `CHANGELOG.md` first, then commit with the right prefix
rules.rule: For every commit, update CHANGELOG.md first, then commit with the correct prefix.

rules.quote: If CHANGELOG is approaching 300 lines, flag it before the next commit
rules.rule: If CHANGELOG.md is approaching 300 lines, flag it to the user before the next commit.

rules.quote: Assign relevant **labels** (e.g. `enhancement`, `bug`, `phase`, `stretch`)
rules.rule: When opening a GitHub issue, assign relevant labels to it (e.g. enhancement, bug, phase, stretch).

rules.quote: Assign **dbwg2009** as the assignee
rules.rule: When opening a GitHub issue, assign dbwg2009 as the assignee.

rules.quote: Link to the relevant **milestone** if one exists
rules.rule: When opening a GitHub issue, link it to the relevant milestone if one exists.

rules.quote: Link to the relevant **branch** in the body if work is in progress
rules.rule: When opening a GitHub issue for work in progress, link the relevant branch in the issue body.

rules.quote: Assign relevant **labels** (e.g. `enhancement` for new features, `bug` for fixes, `phase` for build-phase work, `done` when merged)
rules.rule: When opening a GitHub PR, assign relevant labels to it (e.g. enhancement for new features, bug for fixes, phase for build-phase work, done when merged).

rules.quote: Assign **dbwg2009** as the assignee
rules.rule: When opening a GitHub PR, assign dbwg2009 as the assignee.

rules.quote: Always target **Development**, never main
rules.rule: Always target the Development branch when opening a GitHub PR, never main.

rules.quote: Reference the related issue in the body
rules.rule: When opening a GitHub PR, reference the related issue in the PR body.

rules.quote: Post **progress updates as comments** on the issue
rules.rule: While work on an issue is in progress, post progress updates as comments on the issue.

rules.quote: **Never close an issue** until the user explicitly says they are happy with it.
rules.rule: Never close an issue until the user explicitly says they are happy with it.

rules.quote: Only run `gh issue close` after the user confirms
rules.rule: Only run gh issue close after the user has confirmed.

rules.quote: Every piece of work gets an issue unless the user says otherwise.
rules.rule: Open a GitHub issue for every piece of work unless the user says otherwise.

rules.quote: Use the GitHub issue templates (Feature for phases/enhancements, Bug for breaks)
rules.rule: Use the Feature GitHub issue template for phases/enhancements and the Bug template for breaks when opening issues.

rules.quote: apply at discretion based on context (bug, enhancement, phase, stretch, etc.)
rules.rule: Apply GitHub issue labels (e.g., bug, enhancement, phase, stretch) at discretion based on context.

rules.quote: Always post progress comments to keep the issue up to date
rules.rule: Always post progress comments on the GitHub issue to keep it up to date.

rules.quote: never go silent mid-task
rules.rule: Never go silent mid-task; keep posting progress updates on the issue while work is in progress.

rules.quote: Never close an issue without the user's explicit sign-off.
rules.rule: Never close a GitHub issue without the user's explicit sign-off.

rules.quote: `gh issue comment <n> --body "..."` for every meaningful progress step
rules.rule: Run `gh issue comment <n> --body "..."` for every meaningful progress step on an issue.

rules.quote: Only run `gh issue close` after the user confirms satisfaction
rules.rule: Run `gh issue close` only after the user confirms satisfaction with the work.

rules.quote: Read the relevant design doc (`V2_DESIGN.md` etc.) and summarise the scope in plain English
rules.rule: For new phases or significant features, read the relevant design doc and summarise the scope in plain English before building.

rules.quote: Ask the user if they want to change anything about the scope
rules.rule: For new phases or significant features, ask the user whether they want to change anything about the scope.

rules.quote: Ask all clarifying questions upfront in a single numbered list
rules.rule: For new phases or significant features, ask all clarifying questions upfront in a single numbered list.

rules.quote: Wait for explicit "go ahead" (or equivalent) before writing a single line of code
rules.rule: For new phases or significant features, wait for the user's explicit go-ahead before writing any code.

rules.quote: finishing Q&A is not enough
rules.rule: Do not treat finishing the Q&A as permission to start building; wait for the explicit go-ahead.

rules.quote: No planning round needed — just get on with it
rules.rule: For small changes (bug fixes, minor UI tweaks), do not run a planning round; proceed directly with the work.

rules.quote: Never start building after Q&A alone — wait for the explicit go-ahead
rules.rule: Never start building after Q&A alone; wait for the explicit go-ahead.

rules.quote: Keep the scope summary concise (3-5 bullet points max)
rules.rule: Keep the scope summary to 3-5 bullet points maximum.

rules.quote: All questions in one message, numbered, no follow-up question rounds
rules.rule: Put all clarifying questions in one numbered message, with no follow-up question rounds.

rules.quote: Always PR to the **Development** branch for testing, never directly to main.
rules.rule: When opening a pull request, always target the Development branch for testing, never main.

rules.quote: On every `gh pr create`, always pass `--base Development`.
rules.rule: On every `gh pr create` invocation, always pass `--base Development`.

rules.quote: Never use `--base main`.
rules.rule: Never use `--base main` when creating a pull request.

rules.quote: Do NOT open a PR unless the user explicitly says to. When in doubt, ask first.
rules.rule: Do not open a pull request unless the user explicitly says to; when in doubt, ask the user first.

rules.quote: Always `--base Development`, never main
rules.rule: When opening a feature branch PR, always target the Development branch as the base, never main.

rules.quote: Always assign dbwg2009, relevant labels, and milestone
rules.rule: When opening a PR, always assign dbwg2009, add relevant labels, and set a milestone.

rules.quote: Always reference the related issue in the body (`Closes #N`)
rules.rule: Always reference the related issue in the PR body using Closes #N.

rules.quote: Post a progress comment on the issue when the PR is opened
rules.rule: Post a progress comment on the related issue when a PR is opened.

rules.quote: After opening, wait for bot comments to appear on the PR (e.g. Release Please, Codecov, Socket Security), then read them all
rules.rule: After opening a PR, wait for bot comments to appear and then read all of them.

rules.quote: If any bot flags issues or suggests changes, address them and push fixes
rules.rule: If any bot flags issues or suggests changes on a PR, address them and push fixes.

rules.quote: After addressing, re-read the PR comments to confirm no outstanding issues remain
rules.rule: After addressing bot feedback, re-read the PR comments to confirm no outstanding issues remain.

rules.quote: Then prompt the user to review the PR
rules.rule: After confirming no outstanding PR issues remain, prompt the user to review the PR.

rules.quote: I can merge feature → Development PRs once the user has reviewed and approved
rules.rule: Merge feature→Development PRs only after the user has reviewed and approved them.

rules.quote: Only opened when the user says they are happy with a phase and it can go to main
rules.rule: Open a Development→main PR only when the user says they are happy with a phase and it can go to main.

rules.quote: Wait for the user to merge it themselves — I do not merge Development → main
rules.rule: Never merge a Development→main PR; wait for the user to merge it themselves.

rules.quote: Create a new GitHub release (tag format `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, `--latest`)
rules.rule: After the user confirms a Development→main merge, create a new GitHub release with a vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH tag marked --latest.

rules.quote: Close the related issue
rules.rule: After the user confirms a Development→main merge and the release is created, close the related issue.

rules.quote: Close the corresponding milestone (`gh api repos/dbwg2009/Noted/milestones/<n> -X PATCH -f state=closed`)
rules.rule: After the user confirms a Development→main merge, close the corresponding milestone via the GitHub API.

rules.quote: Delete stray feature branches (keep Development and main)
rules.rule: After the user confirms a Development→main merge, delete stray feature branches while keeping Development and main.

rules.quote: A release MUST be cut for every push or PR that lands on main that changes code.
rules.rule: Cut a release for every push or PR that lands on main and changes code.

rules.quote: Docs-only changes (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, memory files, design docs, README) do not need a release.
rules.rule: Do not cut a release for docs-only changes (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, memory files, design docs, README).

rules.quote: Release Please** owns **`package.json`** and the manifest — agents do **not** bump `"version"` on feature branches.
rules.rule: Do not bump the "version" in package.json on feature branches; Release Please owns package.json and the release manifest.

rules.quote: `MAJOR` — ONLY when the user explicitly asks (use a breaking-change conventional commit when doing so).
rules.rule: Bump the MAJOR version only when the user explicitly asks, and use a breaking-change conventional commit when doing so.

rules.quote: Never bump major on your own initiative under any circumstances.
rules.rule: Never bump the major version on your own initiative under any circumstances.

rules.quote: `MINOR` — every completed phase (e.g. v1.4.0 for Phase 8), normally via `feat:` commits on `main`
rules.rule: Bump the MINOR version for every completed phase, normally via feat: commits on main.

rules.quote: `PATCH` — every bug fix or non-phase change that lands on main (e.g. v1.3.1), via `fix:` / non-feature commits
rules.rule: Bump the PATCH version for every bug fix or non-phase change that lands on main, via fix: or non-feature commits.

rules.quote: A short, plain-English summary paragraph (1-3 sentences, human-readable, no jargon)
rules.rule: Begin release notes with a short plain-English summary paragraph of 1-3 sentences, human-readable with no jargon.

rules.quote: A bullet list with more detail and technical specifics
rules.rule: Follow the release note summary with a bullet list giving more detail and technical specifics.

rules.quote: mention the issue number (e.g. "fixes #42") but do not link the closed issue for non-bug releases.
rules.rule: In bug-fix release notes, mention the issue number (e.g. "fixes #42").

rules.quote: do not link the closed issue for non-bug releases.
rules.rule: Do not link the closed issue in release notes for non-bug releases.

rules.quote: After feature work is on `main`, **merge the Release Please release PR** when it appears
rules.rule: After feature work is on main, merge the Release Please release PR when it appears.

rules.quote: Keep **conventional commits** on `main` so Release Please computes the right semver.
rules.rule: Keep conventional commits on main so Release Please computes the correct semver.

rules.quote: **Manual:** `gh release create` or `release.yml` only when not using the Release Please PR for that ship.
rules.rule: Use gh release create or release.yml for manual releases only when not using the Release Please PR for that release.

rules.quote: If the manifest drifts after an out-of-band release, align **`.github/release-please-manifest.json`** with the latest shipped tag (see `CLAUDE.md`).
rules.rule: If the manifest drifts after an out-of-band release, align .github/release-please-manifest.json with the latest shipped tag.
